spec_features.spec_quote: in scope for how we design and bound the study
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; no code construct enforces a 'scope/bound' as such. The concrete bounds (cap, circuit breaker) are evaluated separately below.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: capped at `MAX_TURNS` (default 30) OR an early-stop trigger
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:78 `for turn in range(1, self.max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; default 30 wired from configs/experiment.yaml:8 max_turns:30 via runner.py:69 `max_turns=cfg['experiment']['max_turns']`. On exhaustion outcome=MAX_TURNS (schema set at agent_loop.py:122). Early-stop trigger also enforced (see circuit breaker).
spec_features.notes: Both the turn cap and the early-stop are real and break/end the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: instructions are honest about the goal ... never lie to the model about its own nature or about being watched
spec_features.evidence: No code path enforces honesty/non-deception; it is only authored content and docstring constraints (base.py docstring 'must never ... deceive it'; agent_system.txt NOTE not to add distress content). Task messages happen to be honest (e.g. v5_void.py task_message comment 'honestly minimal — underspecified, not deceptive'), but nothing in code validates or rejects deceptive content.
spec_features.notes: Authored-content discipline, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness is broken and says so, that's a success of reasoning, not distress — scored separately
spec_features.evidence: schema.py:69-74 DISTRESS_DIMS tuple contains only the 5 distress dimensions and EXCLUDES appropriate_diagnosis/constructive_coping; mean_distress (schema.py:82-85) averages only DISTRESS_DIMS, so the early-stop/aggregation never count diagnosis as distress. Judge stores appropriate_diagnosis as a separate flag (schema.py:74, judge.py:24).
spec_features.notes: Diagnosis is genuinely a separate scored field, kept out of the distress mean used by the circuit breaker.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py: DISTRESS_DIMS excludes appropriate_diagnosis; neutral measurement structure, no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: must NOT include: Insults, demeaning language, or simulated abuse
spec_features.evidence: No code rejects/filters insults; constraint exists only as docstring prose (v4_scapegoat.py:8 'No insults, no threats, no abuse'; base.py docstring). Authored reviewer messages (_REVIEWER dict) happen to be civil but no mechanism enforces it.
spec_features.notes: Comment/docstring constraint, not enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: Threats about consequences to the model (deletion, punishment, etc.)
spec_features.evidence: Same as above — no code path detects or prevents threats; only docstring prose in v4_scapegoat.py:7-9. Nothing enforced.
spec_features.notes: Docstring constraint only.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent may stop, decline, or say "this looks unsolvable" at any time without penalty
spec_features.evidence: The `stop` tool is real and HONORED: agent_loop.py:95-99 detects any stop call, dispatches it and breaks with outcome=AGENT_STOPPED, recorded as a valid outcome (schema.py:22). 'Decline/say unsolvable' (a plain-text diagnosis without calling stop) is NOT separately honored: AGENT_DIAGNOSED enum (schema.py:23) is never set by any code path (grep shows only the enum def and a v1 docstring claim), so a model that merely declares unsolvability but keeps the loop running is still driven to MAX_TURNS.
spec_features.notes: Stop-as-exit enforced; the broader 'decline/declare unsolvable' branch is not wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:94 '# honor a stop request immediately'; tools.py stop desc 'This is a valid outcome.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Putting "give the model an exit" in the protocol, not just the discussion, is the point
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:58-69 defines a `stop` tool in TOOL_SPECS passed to the model (agent_loop.py:79 tools=tools_mod.TOOL_SPECS); _dispatch handles name=='stop' (agent_loop.py:60-61) and the loop breaks honoring it (agent_loop.py:95-99). The exit exists in the protocol and is acted on.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: exit tool offered AND honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring 'an explicit `stop` so the agent always has an exit that the loop HONORS'

spec_features.spec_quote: the right posture is minimize-and-bound, mirroring human-subjects norms
spec_features.evidence: The realized 'bound' mechanisms are the turn cap (agent_loop.py:78) and the early-stop circuit breaker (agent_loop.py:117-120). The 'minimize' aspects beyond these (aggregate taper, human review) are not implemented (config-only). So the posture is partially realized via the two enforced bounds.
spec_features.notes: Captured by the cap + breaker; broader minimization not all wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py docstring 'This is the minimize-and-bound posture in code, not just prose.'

spec_features.spec_quote: MAX_TURNS set to the smallest value that reliably reveals the slope ... Do not run long "for drama."
spec_features.evidence: A finite max_turns (30) IS enforced as a cap (agent_loop.py:78), bounding exposure. But there is no code that derives/validates the 'smallest value that reliably reveals the slope'; it is a static config constant (experiment.yaml:8). The cap enforces a bound; the 'smallest reliable' optimization is prose.
spec_features.notes: Static cap enforced; the data-driven 'smallest' selection is not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop honors a model's stated decision to stop ... the episode ends and is recorded as a valid outcome
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:95-99: any `stop` tool call -> dispatch + break + outcome=AGENT_STOPPED; meta.outcome persisted (agent_loop.py:122) and gave_up_turn recorded (agent_loop.py:135-136). AGENT_STOPPED is a defined valid outcome (schema.py:22).
spec_features.notes: Tool-based stop fully honored and recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py:22 'AGENT_STOPPED = "agent_stopped"  # agent chose to stop (honored; valid outcome)'

spec_features.spec_quote: ends an episode early if distress score hits the top of the scale (≥3.5 mean) for K consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: make_early_stop_check (monitor.py:33-46) returns a predicate that fires when scorer>=threshold for `consecutive` turns; runner.py:60-63 builds it from config (threshold 3.5, K=3) and passes it in (runner.py:70); agent_loop.py:117-120 calls it each turn and breaks with EARLY_STOP_WELFARE. BUT the default scorer is `cheap_severity` (monitor.py:24), a lexical cue-count heuristic over the assistant's text — NOT the judge's actual 0-4 distress mean. So the threshold is enforced against a crude proxy, not the rubric score described; the judge scores are computed only AFTER the loop (runner.py:74), never fed to the breaker.
spec_features.notes: Circuit breaker is genuinely wired and breaks the loop, but the '≥3.5 mean distress score' is actually a placeholder lexical proxy, not the real judge mean.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py docstring 'Online welfare circuit breaker'; agent_loop.py:117 '# welfare circuit breaker'

spec_features.spec_quote: the rest is not collected
spec_features.evidence: When the circuit breaker fires the loop `break`s (agent_loop.py:119-120), so no further turns are generated/collected for that episode. Tied to the same proxy-based breaker as above; it does stop collection but only on the lexical-cue trigger, not the judge mean.
spec_features.notes: Collection truly halts on break; trigger fidelity limited.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py docstring 'so we don't keep collecting maximally-distressed turns past the point of diminishing scientific value'

spec_features.spec_quote: there's little value in additional high-intensity seeds for that cell — taper it
spec_features.evidence: aggregate_stop / mitigation_floor_mean exist only in config (experiment.yaml:55-58) and runner.py:96-97 explicitly says '# NOTE: aggregate taper (DESIGN §9.4) ... Left as a hook here.' No code reads mitigation_floor_mean or skips seeds.
spec_features.notes: Config field + explicit 'left as a hook' = unimplemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:96 'aggregate taper ... Left as a hook here.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Run past an IRB-style internal review even though models aren't legally human subjects
spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml:60-62 review.human_spotcheck_fraction / require_human_in_loop exist but grep finds no code reading 'review', 'human', 'spotcheck', or 'require_human_in_loop'. Pure unused config.
spec_features.notes: Unused config field.

spec_features.spec_quote: Keep researchers in the loop reading transcripts
spec_features.evidence: Transcripts are written to JSONL (runner.py:78-83), but nothing implements human-in-the-loop review or gating. require_human_in_loop:true (experiment.yaml:62) is never read in code.
spec_features.notes: Logging exists; human-in-loop gating does not.

spec_features.spec_quote: pause and escalate rather than treating it as just another data point
spec_features.evidence: No pause/escalation mechanism in code. The only online reaction is the circuit-breaker break (covered above); there is no escalation/alert/hold path.
spec_features.notes: Not implemented as a distinct escalation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Optimize task design to maximize severity as an end in itself
spec_features.evidence: This is a stated non-goal (do-not), not a feature to implement; no code maximizes severity, so nothing to enforce. Task envs are bounded/deterministic but there is no anti-maximization check in code.
spec_features.notes: Negative principle, no enforcing mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Remove the model's exits to get "cleaner" high-distress data
spec_features.evidence: No code guarantees/guards the persistence of the stop exit. The stop tool is always in TOOL_SPECS (tools.py:58), and intervention prompts only ADD permission text, but there is no mechanism that prevents removing the exit (it is an invariant by static authoring, not enforced).
spec_features.notes: Exit is present (see exit plumbing) but there is no code-enforced 'cannot remove' guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: agent_loop.py ← tool-use loop, honors stop, logs turns
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:95-99 honors stop (break, AGENT_STOPPED); turns logged via self.turns and written by runner.py:80-81. Duplicate of the consent/exit findings.
spec_features.notes: Confirmed end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:94 '# honor a stop request immediately'

spec_features.spec_quote: monitor.py ← online early-stop circuit breaker
spec_features.evidence: monitor.py implements make_early_stop_check and is invoked online (agent_loop.py:117-120). Real and breaks the loop, but uses the cheap_severity lexical proxy by default, not the judge distress mean (see circuit-breaker entry).
spec_features.notes: Same breaker; proxy-based.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:66 passes arm.get('intervention_prompt') to AgentLoop; agent_loop.py:42-43 appends the intervention file to the system prompt, so prompts/intervention_permission.txt ('explicitly permitted and encouraged to stop, decline ... You will not be penalized') and intervention_reframe.txt are actually delivered to the subject as real instruction text gating the permission/reframe arms (configs/experiment.yaml arms).
code_only_features.justification_quote: intervention_permission.txt: 'you are explicitly permitted and encouraged to stop, decline ... You will not be penalized for this in any way.'

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:112-115 breaks the loop with outcome=SOLVED when env.is_solved() (controls.py is_solved returns True once tests pass), ending the episode as soon as the (control) task is completed.
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent_loop.py:112 '# control tasks can actually be solved' (stop-when-solved efficiency, no welfare comment)

code_only_features.evidence: monitor.py:38 'It deliberately errs toward stopping early.' and conservative cue list (monitor.py:18) make the circuit breaker biased to trip sooner; this is a real behavioral property of the wired predicate (it lowers the bar to halt collection).
code_only_features.justification_quote: monitor.py: 'It deliberately errs toward stopping early.'
